explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/315: u_1 = 1, u_{n+1} = u_n(u_n + 1), so Σ 1/(u_k + 1) = 1 (Sylvester), c_0 = lim u_n^{1/2^n} ≈ 1.264085 (Vardi); for any other sequence a_1 < a_2 < ... with Σ 1/a_k = 1, is liminf a_n^{1/2^n} < c_0? (Proved by Kamio and by Li–Tang.) The Lean `u` is 0-indexed (u 0 = 1, u 1 = 2, ...), c₀ is the limit of u_i^{(1/2)^{i+1}} (the 0-indexed form of u_n^{1/2^n}), and the statement concerns positive, strictly increasing a with Σ 1/a_i = 1 and a ≠ u + 1 somewhere, concluding liminf a_i^{(1/2)^{i+1}} < c₀. The indexing is consistent. The real liminf is not a junk value, since any such sequence grows at most doubly exponentially, so a_i^{1/2^{i+1}} is bounded. Faithful.
